## Grids and geometry evidence {#sec-ch15-ch03-tests}

Geometry verification checks both local metric formulas and agreement between decomposed blocks.
The latter can fail even when each block has the correct volume; @sec-ch03 explains the geometric construction.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Connect the chapter's claims to executable assertions.

**Data.** Test inputs and thresholds; no new solver measurements.

**Placement.** Verification outside the simulation step.

**Activation.** Select the named tests; this catalogue changes no defaults.

**Guarantee / limits.** Source coverage does not establish a runtime pass.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer distinguishes report checks from solver tests.
:::

### Derivation

The numerical derivations remain in the linked chapter. The error and conservation identities for interpreting
these tests are written out in the opening section of @sec-ch15; this inventory introduces no additional update equation.

### Numerical method

Read the assertion and its registration, then run the selected test in a build of the code pin.
Record device, precision, process count and skipped cases separately. @fig-ch15-evidence shows why an independent
formula check cannot establish that the compiled implementation ran.

: Assertion definitions for this catalogue. {#tbl-ch15-ch03-tests-sources}

The numbered source entries above map directly to the Tests table. CTest registration names and environments
come from `setup_test`, `snapy_add_python_test` and the explicit entries in
{{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}. The `.release` suffix denotes a Release build;
other configurations use their build suffix through `setup_test`
({{< code cmake/macros/macro_setup_test.cmake >}}).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_coordinate.release` | Spherical-polar metric matches reference formulas | rtol = atol = $10^{-12}$ | Source assertion 1 |
| `test_coordinate.release` | Decomposed faces reproduce the undecomposed grid | bitwise equality | Source assertion 2 |
| `test_radial_face_moments.release` | Face centroid shift and second moment match exact integrals | relative $10^{-14}$ | Source assertion 3 |
| `test_cubed_sphere_cell_volume_python` | Shell-volume sum, radial divergence and rest checks | per assertion in `main` | Source assertion 4 |
| `test_cubed_sphere_exchange.release` | Subdivided panels agree with one block after a stage | bitwise equality | Source assertion 5 |
| `test_flux_covariance_seams_python` | Panel-seam conservation, covariance on, cell gravity work | relative drift below $10^{-12}$ | Source assertion 6 |
| `test_x1_seam_split_radial_exact.release` | Split column matches one block; corrected-energy budget closes | gap 0; drift at most $10^{-13}$ | Source assertion 7 |
| `test_x1_seam_split_mp_radial_exact.release` | Two ranks agree with local split and one-block states | relative gap at most $10^{-13}$ | Source assertion 8 |

: Acceptance criteria read from the code pin; no solver pass is claimed. {#tbl-ch15-ch03-tests-assertions}

The seam acceptance test is `main`
({{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py main >}}); `arm_conservation` constructs its measurements.
The switch-off radial-exact registration uses the same `radial_exact_split_gap` assertion with a state-gap
bound of $10^{-13}$ rather than exact equality. It does not assert the corrected-energy drift in that arm.
The seam threshold `DRIFT_TOL` is defined in {{< code tests/test_flux_covariance_seams.py DRIFT_TOL >}}.
`src/snapy_report/ch03/geometry_check.py` checks radial moments, spherical-polar identities, gnomonic transforms,
Morton order and the interpolation slide bound independently of snapy.

### Limits

A panel subdivision in one process is not an MPI result. The selected geometry and exchange assertions do not
establish every corner stencil or every curvature source. The independent slide bound does not execute the
exchange. See @sec-ch12-matrix for configurations needing runtime evidence.
